Not a WONTFIX. Closed by 081356ea; all three mutants hand-verified killed.

My reasoning for filing it was wrong in a specific way worth recording: I argued producedAt had to be OBSERVED -- set by the signing library at signing time, unknowable before the response exists -- and concluded it would take an iterate-until-stable loop to land on a validity edge. It does not have to be observed, it can be WRITTEN. Build the response, rebuild its ResponseData at the DER level with producedAt replaced, re-sign with the responder key the generator holds. That is the same surgery dup-ext/gen.py has used since it needed a certificate cryptography refuses to emit, and I had used it twice the same day.

tests/fixtures/ocsp-produced-at/: four responses over two responder certificates, each pair one second apart in producedAt and identical otherwise. gen.py checks each spliced response parses, carries the producedAt asked for, and verifies under its own embedded certificate.

The lesson generalises: when a fixture needs a field the builder will not set, the question is not whether the builder can be coaxed into setting it but whether the field is inside something this generator can re-sign.
